json.title: checks.freshness overrides parses but nothing consumes it (N2 of #1620)

labels.name: decided
labels.description: An owner decision is recorded on the issue; do not re-litigate the approach

json.body:
#1435 named two `rocky.toml` surfaces that parse and validate while nothing reads them. A systematic sweep of all 24 top-level `RockyConfig` fields and their sub-fields found **three more**. All three are sub-fields, not whole sections, and each is documented as if it worked.

Verified on `main` at `c32f28f9`, with a second independent pass.

## N1 — `[cache.schemas] replicate` (strongest)

**Claim in the docs:** `docs/src/content/docs/reference/configuration.md:923` and `:930` — "Replicate the schema cache via `[state]` sync", `replicate = true # opt in to share cache via the remote state backend`. Also in `schemas/rocky_project.schema.json:3631`.

**What happens:** nothing. Setting it to `true` changes neither sync leg.

- **Upload.** `engine/crates/rocky-core/src/state_sync.rs:2341` — `upload_state()` hard-codes `crate::state::LOCAL_ONLY_TABLE_NAMES`, which contains `"schema_cache"` (`engine/crates/rocky-core/src/state.rs:288`). The override `upload_state_with_excluded_tables` (`state_sync.rs:2391`) exists and its own doc at `:2338` says *"Use `upload_state_with_excluded_tables` to override the default when `[cache.schemas] replicate = true` is configured"* — and it has **no caller outside `state_sync.rs`** (one internal call and one test).
- **Download.** `engine/crates/rocky-cli/src/api.rs:1250` documents that `download_state` unconditionally preserves local-only tables.

```
$ grep -rn --include='*.rs' "\.replicate\b" engine/crates engine/rocky
# every hit is a #[cfg(test)] assertion inside config.rs, or a struct
# literal WRITING `replicate: false` (source_schemas.rs:147,
# schema_cache_writer.rs:189). Zero production reads.
```

The implementation hook was built and never wired: the same shape as #1435's grace-period half.

## N2 — `[pipeline.<name>.checks.freshness] overrides`

**Claim in the docs:** `configuration.md:386` shows `{ threshold_seconds = N, overrides = { ... } }` with no caveat. In `schemas/rocky_project.schema.json:1267`.

**What happens:** the check reads only the scalar. `engine/crates/rocky-cli/src/commands/run.rs:5057`:

```rust
let mut check = checks::check_freshness(lag, freshness_cfg.threshold_seconds);
check.severity = freshness_cfg.severity;
```

`check_freshness` (`engine/crates/rocky-core/src/checks.rs:440`) takes one threshold; there is no per-schema lookup on the path. The engine admits the gap internally at `engine/crates/rocky-cli/src/output.rs:171` — *"Per-schema `overrides` … are intentionally not exposed yet"* — but the user-facing page does not carry that caveat. The field is `deny_unknown_fields`-parsed and folded into the config-snapshot hash, so it looks live.

## N3 — `[schedule] poll_interval_seconds`

**Claim in the docs:** `configuration.md:573` — `poll_interval_seconds = 15 # resident-loop cadence; not consumed by the one-shot rocky tick`. That caveat names the wrong exemption: the resident loop does not consume it either.

**What happens:** nothing reads `config.schedule.poll_interval_seconds`. The only production read of `config.schedule.*` anywhere is `timezone` (`engine/crates/rocky-core/src/schedule/reconcile.rs:790`, `schedule_status.rs:91`, `validate.rs:837`).

The cadence comes from the CLI flag only — `engine/crates/rocky-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:155`:

```rust
poll_interval: poll_interval_seconds        // the --poll-interval-seconds arg
    .map(std::time::Duration::from_secs)
    .unwrap_or(crate::commands::scheduler::DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL),
```

The "reserved for a later phase" defence does not hold: `rocky serve --scheduler` shipped, and its loop re-reads `load_rocky_config(config_path)` on every tick (`scheduler/mod.rs:258`) while the interval stays frozen at spawn (`mod.rs:152`).

**Caveat, stated plainly:** the default (15) equals `DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL`, so the key is inert only for a user who *changes* it. That is still the whole point of setting it.

## Checked and deliberately not reported

- `PolicyRule::conditions` (`config.rs:3110`) is unread but **self-documented** as *"Parsed and ignored — captured as opaque JSON so a config authored against a later version still loads."* A deliberate forward-compatibility hatch, not this defect.
- `[pipeline.*.target.governance] auto_create_schemas` was reported under #1435 and **withdrawn** after a baseline delta showed it works. Not re-reported.

## What to do

Each needs the same call #1435 made, per field: wire it, or refuse it loudly with a message naming the remedy. Silently accepting a key that does nothing is the defect, and a docs-only caveat is not a fix — a `deny_unknown_fields` parser that accepts a key is a promise.

N1 is the one to take first: it has a positive doc claim, a schema entry, a built-but-unreachable implementation hook, and both sync legs hard-coded against it.

Refs #1435

## N1 has shipped. Two of the three remain — re-verified on `main` @ `8e26660e`.

The title still says three. It is two, and N1 was the one this issue recommended taking first, so anyone picking this up from the summary would start on the part that is already done.

### N1 — `[cache.schemas] replicate` — **FIXED**, in #1675

Both sync legs are wired, and the hook this issue described as built-but-unreachable now has production callers.

```
                            when this was filed          on main @ 8e26660e
  cache.schemas.replicate   every hit was #[cfg(test)]   ~18 production reads
  upload leg                LOCAL_ONLY_TABLE_NAMES        threaded through
                            hard-coded                    replicate_schema_cache
```

Read by `run.rs` (5 sites), `apply.rs` (4), `policy.rs`, `gc.rs`, `load.rs`, `fulfill_api.rs`. `policy.rs:473` and `gc.rs:1731` resolve it into a `replicate_schema_cache` flag and thread it to the sync call, which is exactly the override path this issue said had no caller outside `state_sync.rs`.

### N2 — `[pipeline.<name>.checks.freshness] overrides` — **still live**

`check_freshness` is unchanged at `engine/crates/rocky-core/src/checks.rs:600`:

```rust
pub fn check_freshness(lag_seconds: u64, threshold_seconds: u64) -> CheckResult
```

One scalar threshold, no per-schema lookup. `grep -rn '\.overrides\b'` across `run.rs` and `checks.rs` returns nothing. The key still parses under `deny_unknown_fields` and still folds into the config-snapshot hash.

### N3 — `[schedule] poll_interval_seconds` — **still live**

Nothing reads `config.schedule.poll_interval_seconds`. The only occurrences outside its own definition (`config.rs:4989`) are the CLI flag in `serve.rs:127` and `serve.rs:220`. The cadence still comes from `--poll-interval-seconds` alone, and the resident loop still freezes it at spawn while re-reading the rest of the config every tick.

### What this changes about the issue

The recommendation at the bottom — "N1 is the one to take first" — is spent. Of what is left, **N3 is the cheaper and more clear-cut**: one key, one read to add, and the doc caveat at `configuration.md:573` currently names the wrong exemption, so the page is wrong either way. N2 is a feature (per-schema thresholds), not a wiring gap, and its docs already carry an internal admission at `output.rs:171`.

Both still fail the standard #1435 set: a `deny_unknown_fields` parser that accepts a key is a promise.

Refs #1435, #1675

Reopened: **N3 is done, N2 is not.**

PR #1868 wired `[schedule] poll_interval_seconds` and its commit said `Closes #1620 N3` — GitHub parsed the closing keyword and ignored the qualifier, so the whole issue closed. My mistake; a qualified `Closes` is still a `Closes`.

**What shipped (N3):** the resident scheduler now reads the key. Precedence is `--poll-interval-seconds` → `[schedule] poll_interval_seconds` → built-in, extracted into `resolved_poll_interval` with four tests. The reference page's caveat, which named the wrong exemption, is corrected.

**What remains (N2):** `[pipeline.<name>.checks.freshness] overrides`. `check_freshness` still takes a single scalar threshold (`rocky-core/src/checks.rs:600`) and no per-schema lookup exists on the path. It still parses under `deny_unknown_fields` and still folds into the config-snapshot hash.

N2 is a feature (per-schema thresholds), not a wiring gap — which is why it did not come along with N3.

N2 is blocked on a decision, and the code says so in its own words. Verified on `main` @ `8b5c4522`.

`output.rs:169-172`:

> Per-schema `overrides` from `rocky_core::config::FreshnessConfig` are intentionally **not exposed yet** — the override-key semantics need to be nailed down before integrations can rely on them.

So this is not "wire the key up". It is "decide what the key means", after which the wiring is small.

## What the key could mean, and what the evidence says

**Which schema?** The doc comment's example is `raw__us_west__shopify`. Per `AGENTS.md` the schema pattern is `src__{tenant}__{regions}__{source}` for SOURCE and `raw__{regions}__{source}` for TARGET — so the example is a **target** schema. That also matches where the check runs: `run.rs:7056` iterates `freshness_batch_refs`, whose `TableRef` is the target.

**Exact or glob?** The field is `HashMap<String, u64>`, whose keys are exact by construction, but the doc calls it "a schema pattern" and says it applies "for matching schemas". Those disagree. A glob would need a matcher — one exists for `[[table_overrides]]` — and would need a precedence rule for two patterns matching one schema.

## The two honest ends

**Wire it** — target schema, exact key, `overrides.get(schema).unwrap_or(threshold_seconds)`. Both emit sites must use the resolved value: the measured check at `run.rs:7062` and the `freshness_not_evaluated` fallback at `:7073`, which also reports a threshold. Reporting one threshold and applying another is the failure this would otherwise introduce. Exposing it in `FreshnessConfigOutput` is separate and additive — the check can honour overrides without `discover` listing them.

**Remove it** — the key stops parsing, and nothing promises what it cannot do. Allowed before 2.0, and it is the smaller change, but it deletes a documented feature.

I would **wire it, exact, on the target schema**: it is what the example key already looks like, it needs no matcher and no precedence rule, and a glob can be added later without breaking an exact key. But this is a config contract on a `deny_unknown_fields` surface that folds into the config-snapshot hash, so it is your call rather than mine — which is exactly what `output.rs` was waiting for.

## What I am least confident about

Whether "target schema" is right for a check whose *purpose* is to notice a stale SOURCE. Freshness measures `MAX(ts)` on the target, so keying on the target is what the data supports. But an operator thinking "the shopify connector is slow, give it a longer budget" is thinking in source terms, and one source can fan out to several target schemas — under a target key they would have to write the override several times, and would have no way to say "every schema fed by shopify". If that is the real use, the key wants to be the source and the example in the doc comment is misleading.

## What I think is being missed

Whichever way this goes, the key is already inside the config-snapshot hash. Changing an override today changes the hash and therefore the fingerprint that gates a governed run, so an operator can already cause a re-plan by editing a field that does nothing. That is not new with this issue, but it means "the key is inert" is not quite true — it is inert for the CHECK and live for the FINGERPRINT, which is the worse of the two states to leave it in.

Refs #1435, #1675

**Decided (2026-09-17): remove `[pipeline.<name>.checks.freshness] overrides`.** Whether the key should name the target or the source schema is unresolved, so the key stops parsing instead of promising a contract. Re-add it when someone asks, with that question answered.
